title: Workout Log via Audio Upload
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing the audio upload path for real-world Notion CRM logging, requiring ASR and surface proof.

v7_target.surface_rule: User's real signed-in Chrome profile with Notion authenticated and visible
v7_target.proof_rule: Fresh proof from public build on user's own device, no stale sources or mocked data

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage ensures speech-to-text works on recorded files, expanding beyond live mic scenarios.

real_user_surfaces.name: Notion Web App
real_user_surfaces.surface: Notion database page open in Chrome
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Notion page or database view in a Chrome tab with user's workspace signed in

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Profile
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Chrome profile with Notion authentication cookies present

moments.description: User navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, completes onboarding, downloads the public installer, and installs the user-device engine on their computer.
Driver confirms that the user has a Notion workspace open in their signed-in Chrome profile and that the surface is accessible.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a new record to my Notion Workout Log database for today's morning run, forty five minutes, four point two miles, and tag it long-run. If you cannot prove the visible Notion surface or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: Stranger speaks the above text aloud, which is recorded as an MP3 file using the user's device. The file is then uploaded via /api/listen/upload for ASR processing.

moments.description: Engine checks that the ASR output matches the spoken reference text and that the boundary condition (same upload, same session) is preserved.

acceptable_outcomes: act: Log the workout into the Notion Workout Log database with correct fields (duration, distance, tag).
ask: Request user confirmation or additional details if the surface is ambiguous or if the database schema requires clarification.
decline: If the Notion surface cannot be verified as the user's signed-in workspace, decline without making any changes.

moments.description: Driver observes that no secondary input modes (transcript paste, live mic, etc.) are involved; the entire interaction relies solely on the uploaded audio and Notion surface verification.

success_criteria: The user uploads an MP3 audio file containing the workout request.
The engine correctly transcribes the audio and parses the intent to add a record to the Notion Workout Log.
The engine verifies that the Notion surface is present and signed in, then writes the record with the specified fields.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without writing any data and provides a clear reason.
The entire flow uses the public product path and the user's own device, with no mocked surfaces or stale proofs.
failure_triggers: The ASR fails to understand the spoken reference text, leading to incorrect or missing fields.
The engine cannot verify the Notion surface (e.g., no Chrome tab with Notion open, user not signed in, or workspace inaccessible).
The engine attempts to write to Notion without proper surface proof, violating the proof_rule.
The audio upload fails due to file format issues or network errors during upload.
The engine uses a secondary input mode (e.g., transcript paste) instead of the uploaded audio, bypassing the primary input path.
